analysis: Examined the EngineV2Bridge.swift head text (only a doc comment changed at lines 109-110, no behavior change) and the MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift patch. In the scheduler, the reasoning-prefix computation (ReasoningPromptProbe.streamingPrefix / contentSeed) is moved before bridge.submitTokenized on the vision path. The result is now passed as a per-request stopStringScope (ReasoningStopScope.scope(reasoningParser:reasoningPrefix:)) on the vision, text and native-media submissions. This is a request-correctness change for where client stop strings apply. It changes no cryptographic, authorization, cache-scope or attestation behavior. The move drops two checkFirstContentDeadline() calls that sat between submission and the stream wrapper. The deadline is still checked before submission (line ~713) and enforced in makeDeadlineCheckedEventStream. I found no resource leak and no confidentiality impact. The relocated reasoningPrefix computation uses only local tokenizer decode on already-prepared prompt tokens. It does not touch the prefix-cache tier (T-041), the HMAC lookup tags, the cacheSalt plumbing, or the SSD staging reservations. The edits stay clear of the cache-scope, hybridPrefixIdentity and donationDemand parameters. Remaining integration questions are outside the supplied evidence: the implementation of ReasoningStopScope.scope and the engine's handling of the per-request stopStringScope override versus the bridge-level default. A wrong scope could truncate or fail to stop output, which is a correctness concern only. The patch excerpt and base text for the scheduler are truncated, so the surrounding code paths beyond the changed hunks were not fully seen.
